review.summary: I reviewed only the three files you sent and found no BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR issues. Quick publish now runs only for a project that is still a draft and has never been published (status "draft" with no publishedAt). If the project was already published, it is reported as ready and not published again. Any other status, or a page with past publish history, is sent to the normal manager screens. On retry, the project is only auto-published if the page is untouched: still at revision 1 and never taken offline. The action file checks the same two things before it publishes the page. The project publish check now lives in a shared helper, and it still requires a priced active product and a currently verified vendor payment method. Its last update (updateMany) also still excludes archived projects, and the quick path writes its own audit entry when it publishes the project. On retry, a supplied title is checked only against the stored page name, so renaming the video does not cause a conflict. The new templates use the "registration_confirmed" and "live_reminder" triggers and are linked directly to the live session and its reminder rule. The thank-you page asks the user to confirm their email, and the confirmation email says it is already confirmed, which matches confirmation happening after verification. I couldn't check what isn't in these files: canPublishSalesProject, the old publish endpoint (to confirm it now calls this helper), how publishLandingPage checks ownership, the verify route, and the send code. I'm relying on your description for those. Two minor points, too small to list as findings: (1) the final project update doesn't re-check that the project is still a never-published draft. If a manager publishes the same project at the same moment, publishedAt can be overwritten and two audit entries written, with no other effect. (2) If the page is published outside the main transaction and that fails, the project stays published while the page doesn't; the user gets a needs_attention message and retrying with the same request fixes it. No findings does not mean tests passed: the expanded 13-check Postgres run was still in progress and is not reported as passing.
